payload.taxonomy: CouncilOS / Implementation Council failure-mode taxonomy (trusted-user environment)

critical_findings.finding: Evidence pointer objects in decision_log appear non-compliant with the stated single standard (RFC 6901 evidence pointer object structure). The plan requires evidence pointers to be exactly {artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note}, but decision_log evidence pointers include extra/nonstandard fields (e.g., candidate_id, artifact_id, quote). This can cause strict validators to fail or, worse, inconsistent downstream parsing/trace validation.

closure.closure_target: Before candidate is promoted to canonical; must pass an evidence-pointer linter gate
closure.required_fix: Normalize all evidence pointer occurrences to the exact required object shape; move any extra fields (quotes, local IDs) into allowed fields (e.g., note) or adjacent non-evidence metadata fields explicitly permitted by schema; add validator that rejects unknown keys inside evidence pointer objects.

critical_findings.finding: Reviewer role cannot produce required findings artifacts under current tool_policy: Review stage restrictions set artifact_write=deny and workspace_write=deny, but architecture/requirements require reviewers to emit review_findings.json (findings-only). This creates a dead-end stage or forces policy bypass (writing via noncanonical channels), undermining governance and auditability.

closure.closure_target: Prior to implementing stage tool permissions; must be consistent before acceptance tests are finalized
closure.required_fix: Amend Review stage policy to allow artifact_write for a tightly-scoped allowlist of findings-only artifact types (e.g., review_findings.json) while still prohibiting patch/code writes; add orchestrator enforcement that reviewers can only write those artifact types and cannot write patchsets or modify canonical planning artifacts.

critical_findings.finding: Stage-model inconsistency across requirements/acceptance tests vs chosen O1 architecture/tool_policy risks invalid stage sequencing, missing stage_handoffs, and broken checkpoint/resume invariants. Requirements/ATs specify minimum stages Intake → Generate → Validate → Review → Judge → Freeze, but architecture and tool_policy introduce WorkPlanning and PatchApply (and also IntegrateAndValidate). Without a canonical stage taxonomy and mapping, validators may reject legitimate runs or allow ungoverned transitions.

closure.closure_target: Before schema/validator implementation of the state machine and before publishing acceptance tests
closure.required_fix: Define a single canonical stage enumeration and explicitly update: (1) R4 and AT4 pass criteria to match O1 stage list, or (2) provide a deterministic mapping showing that WorkPlanning/PatchApply are sub-stages captured within Generate/Validate (and ensure stage_handoff expectations match). Remove unused stages from tool_policy for O1 or mark them as non-applicable to O1 with validator logic.

critical_findings.finding: Key governance-critical primitives are left as blocking open questions (artifact_ref format, diff format/normalization, deterministic patch selection), but multiple MUST requirements and validators depend on them. If left unresolved, implementations will improvise, causing nondeterminism and breaking audit spine/evidence pointer resolution and patch determinism guarantees.

closure.closure_target: Before freezing the plan package as canonical; block downstream implementation until resolved
closure.required_fix: Convert Q3/Q7/Q8 into explicit normative specs in the plan package (artifact_ref naming/versioning + resolution rules; patchset diff format + normalization; deterministic 'smallest passing repair' computation including byte counting definition); add schema fields and validators that enforce these definitions.

critical_findings.finding: Forbidden/protected path enforcement is specified as mandatory, but the concrete patterns/semantics are undefined (repo_context schema content and enforcement rules remain open). Tool policy also uses placeholders ('policy_defined', 'from_repo_context'), creating a failure mode where protection is effectively non-enforceable or inconsistently enforced across repos, enabling high-blast-radius changes (CI/release/auth configs) despite intended safeguards.

closure.closure_target: Before any patch application tooling is approved; required for safe operation
closure.required_fix: Define repo_context.json protected/forbidden path schema precisely (glob syntax, normalization, precedence, directories vs files, symlink handling), and require repo-specific policy profiles; implement dual enforcement (patch_apply-time + sandbox FS policy) and add an explicit validator that fails if protections are empty/overbroad/ill-formed.

critical_findings.finding: Network is denied across stages by default, but the plan lacks a fully specified deterministic offline dependency strategy (mirrors, allowlists, lockfile rules) and acknowledges open questions on network/dependencies. For many real repos, Validate will fail (cannot fetch deps), triggering repeated retries/escalations and potentially incentivizing ad-hoc permission expansions that reduce reproducibility and security.

closure.closure_target: Before defining default validator gates (R21) for any repo ecosystem; required to avoid systematic dead-on-arrival runs
closure.required_fix: Specify a deterministic dependency policy: mandatory lockfiles, optional offline mirrors/caches, and (if network allowed) strict domain allowlists and recorded provenance; encode policy in repo_context/workspace_context and add validators enforcing pinned dependency resolution and reproducible installs.

critical_findings.finding: Secrets prevention requires scanning/redaction/blocking 'before any artifact is persisted', but the design also requires append-only event logs and extensive artifact emission at each checkpoint. Without an explicit pre-commit scanning pipeline for ALL writes (including event log lines, stage_handoffs, patchsets, snapshots, context packs), secrets can be irreversibly persisted into immutable/append-only stores, creating an unrecoverable compliance incident.

closure.closure_target: Before enabling real artifact persistence (especially append-only logs) in any environment that could see secrets
closure.required_fix: Make the Workspace Gateway/Artifact Store interface enforce a mandatory 'scan-before-store' transaction for every write/append; define how blocked writes are represented without persisting secret material (e.g., store only a classifier label + hash of redacted content); add validator that ensures no write path bypasses scanning.

critical_findings.finding: Deterministic 'smallest passing repair' selection is based only on operations count, bytes changed, and first-generated tie-breaker. This can repeatedly select a patch that passes tests but is higher long-term risk (e.g., weak security posture, maintainability regressions) when multiple candidates pass. The failure mode is subtle technical-debt/security degradation under deterministic but overly narrow optimization criteria.

closure.closure_target: Before finalizing judge/selection logic as part of orchestrator policy; ideally before first production use
closure.required_fix: Add deterministic secondary scoring validators (security/static analysis results, complexity delta, lint/format deltas, forbidden API usage) that can be incorporated into a deterministic selection order; alternatively require HITL when multiple passing candidates differ materially on risk signals.
